You will be accountable to the Board of Directors and the members for the general direction, operation and day-to-day administration of the credit union. You will take responsibility for the staff, oversee the delivery of all services to members and help the credit union continue to grow, while fostering a positive, inspiring and collaborative working environment. Key responsibilities Strategic thinking and leadership Develop the strategic and annual business plans and budgets with the Board of Directors Support the Board in the performance of its duties and report on progress against its strategic goals Lead and develop the senior management team and staff Delivery focus Lead the day-to-day operational management of the business, including financial, investment, credit control, business development, marketing, lending, member service and operations, IT and digital delivery, risk management, compliance and anti-money laundering Continuously improve systems, processes, policies, procedures and efficiency across all functions Take responsibility for all internal and external audits, Central Bank inspections and reporting to the Central Bank Lead the continuous development of the credit union's products and services Lead the planning of the AGM and the statutory audit for the AGM Oversee the IT and technology systems used to deliver services Managing relationships and communications Take responsibility for HR, employee relations, performance management, recruitment and training Maintain a culture of compliance, and make sure the Board and staff know about any new regulatory requirements Lead change management and staff engagement Specialist expertise and self-development Manage performance and carry out performance reviews for all staff Support a culture of self-development for all staff Values and commitment Keep developing the credit union's community-based ethos and values Represent the credit union with key stakeholders and Have at least 5 years at senior management level, managing a diverse range of operations, including compliance and risk management Have exceptional people management and motivation skills Show a genuine interest in the credit union movement and a passion for its values and ethos Know the relevant legislation for credit unions in Ireland Understand not-for-profit organisations and have experience working with and reporting to Boards of Directors Have strong IT and digital transformation skills Have experience driving and implementing continuous improvement and change Qualifications A level 8 business or finance degree and/or other credit union, banking or financial services qualifications Ideally a qualified accountant, or extensive experience preparing accounts and managing bank reconciliations in a financial services business What we're looking for The credit union's competency framework centres on strategic thinking and leadership, a focus on delivery, managing relationships and communications, specialist expertise and self-development, and a drive and commitment to the credit union's values. You will work well with the Board, other credit unions, the Central Bank and other stakeholders, and build trust through honesty, respect and delivering on your commitments. Salary is negotiable depending on experience. The role is office based at Headfort Place, Kells, Co. Meath, and is full-time and permanent. The CEO is also required to attend meetings and represent the credit union at appropriate functions. How to apply Submit a single document containing: A short cover letter or personal statement (maximum two pages) explaining why you want the post and how your qualities, qualifications, knowledge, experience and values meet the requirements A comprehensive CV, including two referees. Referees will only be contacted if you come under consideration The Key Achievements Form (maximum 250 words for each of the five competency areas) Apply to: acarter@morganmckinley.com / simonmorris@morganmckinley.com Selection process Shortlisting is based on the information in your application, so please give a detailed account of your qualifications and experience. Shortlisted candidates will go to a competitive interview, which may include a presentation. Interview dates are fixed, so please make sure you are available. A reference from your current employer will be required before an appointment is recommended. This role is a Pre-Approval Controlled Function (CUPCF-2) for Fitness and Probity under the Central Bank Reform Act 2010 (Credit Unions) Regulations 2013. Successful candidates may also need to complete clearance processes, such as a Health and Character Declaration and any other checks the role requires.

review_candidates.description: Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Join Us as a Clinical Research Associate I – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years. As part of our global team, you’ll have the opportunity to perform and coordinate different aspects of the clinical monitoring and site management process. As a Clinical Research Associate I, you'll conduct remote or on-site visits to assess protocol and regulatory compliance and manage required documentation. You will manage procedures and guidelines from different sponsors and/or monitoring environments (i.e., FSO, FSP, Government, etc.). Acting as a site processes specialist, you will ensure that the trial is conducted in accordance with the approved protocol, ICH-GCP guidelines, applicable regulations, and SOPs to guarantee subjects' rights, well-being, and data reliability. You will ensure audit readiness and develop collaborative relationships with investigational sites. Detailed tasks and responsibilities assigned to your role are outlined in the task matrix. Ensures data accuracy through SDR, SDV and CRF review as applicable through on-site and remote monitoring activities. Assess investigational product through physical inventory and records review. Documents observations in reports and letters in a timely manner using approved business writing standards. Escalates observed deficiencies and issues to clinical management expeditiously and follow all issues through to resolution. May need to maintain regular contact between monitoring visits with investigative sites to confirm that the protocol is being followed, that previously identified issues are being resolved and that the data is being recorded in a timely manner. Conducts monitoring tasks in accordance with the approved monitoring plan. Participates in the investigator payment process. Ensures a shared responsibility with other project team members on issues/findings resolution. Investigates and follows-up on findings as applicable. Participates in investigator meetings as necessary. May help to identify potential investigators in collaboration with the client company to ensure the acceptability of qualified investigative sites. Initiates clinical trial sites according to the relevant procedures to ensure compliance with the protocol and regulatory and ICH GCP obligations, making recommendations where warranted. Performs trial close out and retrieval of trial materials. Ensures that required essential documents are complete and in place, according to ICH-GCP and applicable regulations. Conducts on-site file reviews as per project specifications. Provides trial status tracking and progress update reports to the team as required. Ensures study systems are complete, accurate and updated per agreed study conventions (e.g. Clinical Trial Management System). Facilitates effective communication between investigative sites, the client company and internal project teams through written, oral and/or electronic contacts. Responds to company, client and applicable regulatory requirements/audits/inspections. Maintains and completes administrative tasks such as expense reports and timesheets in a timely manner. Contributes to the project team by assisting in preparation of project publications/tools and sharing ideas/suggestions with team members. Contributes to other project work and initiatives for process improvement, as required. Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor's degree in a life sciences related field or a Registered Nursing certification or equivalent and relevant formal academic / vocational qualification. Minimal clinical monitoring experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job (comparable to 2 years) in a clinical environment where experience is gained in clinical trials, medical terminology, medical research, clinical research or health care or experience in a health sciences field with formal training in medical terminology and anatomy may be considered. Valid driver's license where applicable. In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Basic medical/therapeutic area knowledge and understanding of medical terminology Ability to attain and maintain a working knowledge of ICH GCPs and applicable regulations and procedural documents Good oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with medical personnel Good interpersonal skills Ability to maintain customer focus through the utilization of good listening skills, attention to detail and the ability to perceive customers’ underlying issues Good organizational and time management skills Ability to remain flexibile and adaptable in a wide range of scenarios Well-developed critical thinking skills, including but not limited to: critical mindset, in-depth investigation for appropriate root cause analysis and problem solving Ability to manage Risk Based Monitoring concepts and processes Ability to work in a team or independently as required Good computer skills: solid knowledge of Microsoft Office and the ability to learn appropriate software Good English language and grammar skills Working Conditions and Environment: Work is performed in an office/ laboratory/clinical/and/or home office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment. Frequent drives to site locations. Frequent travel, generally 60-80% but more for some individuals. May also include extended overnight stays. Exposure to biological fluids with potential exposure to infectious organisms. Personal protective equipment required such as protective eyewear, garments and gloves. Exposure to fluctuating and/or extreme temperatures on rare occasions.

Responsabilidades principales •     Plan de auditoría: formular el plan anual de auditoría interna basado en riesgos y someterlo a la aprobación de la Junta Directiva. •     Control interno: evaluar los controles de los procesos financieros, comerciales, de servicios, de compras, inventarios y nómina, en todos los países de operación. •     Información financiera: verificar la confiabilidad de la información que recibe la Junta Directiva y el cumplimiento de las políticas contables y de cierre. •     Políticas y autorizaciones: verificar el cumplimiento de la matriz de autorizaciones, las políticas de precios, descuentos y comisiones, y las reglas de operaciones entre compañías y con partes relacionadas. •     Tecnología y seguridad de la información: evaluar, en coordinación con el CISO y el área de Cumplimiento, los controles de tecnología y de seguridad de la información. •     Prevención del fraude: diseñar y administrar el canal de denuncias y conducir las investigaciones que la Junta Directiva le encomiende. •     Seguimiento: dar seguimiento a las recomendaciones de la auditoría externa, de la auditoría interna y a los requerimientos de la Junta Directiva hasta su cierre. •     Informes: presentar informes periódicos a la Junta Directiva y a su Comité de Finanzas y Auditoría, con hallazgos, riesgos y planes de acción. •     Coordinación: ser el enlace con los auditores externos y con los reguladores, cuando corresponda. •     Equipo: formar y dirigir el equipo de auditoría interna del grupo. Se valorará experiencia previa en firmas internacionales de auditoría. •     Conocimientos técnicos: Normas Globales de Auditoría Interna del Instituto de Auditores Internos (IIA); marco de control interno COSO; gestión de riesgos empresariales; NIIF; prevención y detección de fraude. •     Herramientas: análisis de datos aplicado a la auditoría y conocimiento de SAP u otro ERP. •     Idioma: inglés avanzado, oral y escrito. •     Deseable: certificación CIA (auditor interno certificado), CISA (auditoría de sistemas de información) o CFE (examinador de fraude certificado); conocimiento de ISO/IEC 27001 y de PCI DSS. Comunica con oportunidad y claridad los hallazgos relevantes a cualquier nivel de la organización, incluida la Alta Dirección. •     Enfoque constructivo. Identifica deficiencias y propone soluciones viables; orienta su labor a la mejora de los procesos y no solo a la detección de errores. •     Prudencia y discreción. Maneja con reserva absoluta la información a la que tiene acceso y actúa con mesura en situaciones sensibles. •     Construcción de la función. Establece la metodología, el equipo y los estándares de trabajo de la auditoría interna del grupo, y desarrolla a sus colaboradores. •     Ejemplaridad. Su conducta es irreprochable y refuerza la cultura de integridad y de control en toda la organización. Relacionamiento El Auditor General se relaciona con todos los niveles de la organización.
